creative_direction.narrative_arc: Orbit mystery → ocean energy → rising moisture → condensation heat → circulation → real eye → limits and consequences
creative_direction.voice_and_music: No TTS, voice model, stock music or source audio cleared or generated in issue 037
creative_direction.note: Caption each observational clip with its real event/year. The expedition waves are illustrative, not hurricane footage or a sea-temperature reading. All animations are explanatory schematics, never measured satellite products.

scientific_claims.statement: Tropical cyclones obtain energy from warm ocean heat and moisture; warm water alone is insufficient for formation.
Rising moist air condenses and releases latent heat, supporting convection and cyclone circulation when other conditions are favorable.
Loss of warm ocean heat/moisture over land or cooler water can weaken tropical cyclones; dangerous impacts may persist.

shots.visual: Unmodified approved BlueDotAtlas original intro; preserve its supplied soundtrack.

shots.caption: Tropical Cyclone Oma · ISS / NASA · 2019
shots.visual: ISS Expedition 58 timelapse over the Coral Sea. Respect original 1080×720 (3:2) framing, not fake 16:9 footage; do not silently distort crop. Hook starts after intro fades.

narration.text: From space, a tropical cyclone looks like a giant spiral. Its energy starts below.

shots.caption: North Atlantic expedition · Illustrative waves · NOAA 2021
shots.visual: Actual wind-driven open-sea camera waves from a NOAA Ocean Exploration expedition. Clearly labeled illustrative B-roll: NOT hurricane footage and NOT a sea-surface temperature observation.

narration.text: Warm tropical seas supply heat and moisture. But warm water alone cannot create a hurricane.

shots.caption: Ocean heat + moisture · Schematic
shots.visual: Original vector illustration: simple blue ocean, warm-air/moisture arrows rising. Clearly marked Schematic; no temperature readouts, satellite graphics or invented measurements.

narration.text: Water evaporates from the ocean surface. Rising humid air helps feed the storm's towering clouds.

shots.caption: Condensation releases heat · Schematic
shots.visual: Original vertical section illustration of vapor cooling and condensing into cloud droplets; show released heat without invented numerical measurements.

narration.text: As that air climbs, it cools. Water vapor condenses into droplets, releasing heat into the atmosphere.

shots.caption: Rising air + circulation · Schematic
shots.visual: Conceptual circulation arrows become organized around a diagrammatic center; label only qualitative movement, avoid suggesting warm water alone causes a storm.

narration.text: This released heat supports rising air and circulation, if the atmosphere provides other favorable conditions.

shots.caption: Hurricane Helene · NOAA Hurricane Hunter · 2024
shots.visual: Real WP-3D Orion hurricane-eye footage, with Nick Underwood/NOAA attribution; do not imply same storm as Oma or ocean expedition. Use no original AAC soundtrack before individual clearance.

narration.text: From a hurricane hunter aircraft, the eye reveals how enormous that circulation can become.

shots.caption: Less ocean heat → weaker fuel · Schematic
shots.visual: Clearly schematic ocean-to-land/cooler-water move with weakening heat-flow arrows; show that risks can continue. Original animation, not an observation of Oma/Helene.

narration.text: Over land or cooler seas, storms often weaken. Dangerous impacts can still persist.
